p.src: Now Prefect He, having lured Lu Zhishen into the rear hall, shouted, “Seize him!” A crowd of constables surrounded Lu Zhishen and hustled him below the steps of the hall. Prefect He demanded, “Where did you come from, you bald donkey?” Lu Zhishen replied, “What crime have I committed?” The prefect said, “Tell the truth. Who sent you to assassinate me?” Lu Zhishen said, “I am a monk. Why do you ask me such a thing?” The prefect shouted, “Just now I saw you, bald donkey, meaning to strike my sedan chair with your staff, but then you thought better of it and dared not act. Confess properly, you bald donkey!” Lu Zhishen said, “I never tried to kill you. Why have you seized me and falsely accused an innocent man?” The prefect cursed him: “Who ever heard of a monk calling himself ‘your lord’?” This bald donkey must be one of those bandits who rob and plunder across the five circuits of the western passes. He has come to avenge that scoundrel Shi Jin. He will never confess unless he is beaten. Men, put your backs into beating that bald donkey!” Lu Zhishen cried out, “Do not injure your lord! I will tell you: I am Lu Zhishen, the ‘Flowery Monk,’ a hero of Liangshan Marsh. My death matters little, but when my elder brother Song Gongming hears of it and comes down from the mountain, you had better cut off that donkey’s head of yours at once and send it to him!” Prefect He flew into a rage on hearing this. After having Lu Zhishen tortured for a time, he ordered a great cangue brought, had it nailed around his neck, and sent him down to the condemned prisoners’ jail. At the same time, he reported the matter to the central authorities and requested an explicit ruling; the monk’s staff and戒刀 were sealed away in the prefectural hall.

p.src: The whole prefecture of Huazhou was thrown into an uproar. A young bandit learned the news and raced back up the mountain to report it. Wu Song was aghast. “The two of us came to Huazhou on a mission, and now one of us has been lost. How can I go back and face the other chiefs?” While he was at a loss what to do, a young bandit came up from below and reported, “A chief sent from Liangshan Marsh, called Dai Zong the ‘Divine Traveler,’ is now at the foot of the mountain.” Wu Song hurried down to welcome him and brought him up the mountain. After Dai Zong had exchanged greetings with Zhu Wu and the other two, Wu Song related how Lu Zhishen had ignored their warnings and fallen into the enemy’s hands. Dai Zong was greatly alarmed. “I cannot remain here long! I shall return at once to Liangshan Marsh and inform our elder brother, so that troops and commanders may quickly be sent to the rescue!” Wu Song said, “I shall wait here. I earnestly beg you, brother, to go quickly and return with all haste.” After eating some vegetarian fare, Dai Zong invoked his magic traveling art and set off again for Liangshan Marsh. Within three days, he had reached the stronghold. On meeting the two chiefs, Chao and Song, he told them how Lu Zhishen, attempting to rescue Shi Jin, had tried to assassinate Prefect He and been trapped. When Song Jiang heard the account, he exclaimed in alarm, “Since two of our brothers are in peril, how can we fail to rescue them? We must not delay. We must muster our forces at once and march in three divisions.” Five vanguard commanders were appointed to the front division: Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Lin Chong, Yang Zhi, and Huyan Zhuo. Leading one thousand armored cavalry and two thousand infantry, they were to advance first, opening roads through the mountains and laying bridges wherever they met water; the main division had six chiefs: its commander Song Gongming, the strategist Wu Yong, Zhu Tong, Xu Ning, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao, with two thousand cavalry and infantry; the rear division, charged with the provisions, was brought up by five chiefs—Li Ying, Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, Li Jun, and Zhang Shun—with two thousand cavalry and infantry. Thus a total force of seven thousand men and horses left Liangshan Marsh and marched straight for Huazhou. They pressed on for several days, and after they had passed the halfway point, Dai Zong was sent ahead to notify those on Mount Shaohua. Zhu Wu and the other two prepared pigs, sheep, cattle, and horses, brewed fine wine, and waited for them.

p.src: Now all three divisions of Song Jiang’s army arrived below Mount Shaohua. Wu Song led Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun down the mountain to pay their respects and invite Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and all the chiefs up to the stronghold, where they took their seats. Song Jiang questioned them closely about affairs within the city. Zhu Wu said, “The two chiefs have already been confined in prison by Prefect He. They are merely awaiting the court’s explicit decree and disposal.” Song Jiang said to Wu Yong, “What plan can we devise to rescue Shi Jin and Lu Zhishen?” Zhu Wu said, “Huazhou’s walls encompass a broad area, and its moat is deep and wide. It cannot be taken in haste. Only by coordinating an attack from within and without can we capture it.” Scholar Wu said, “Tomorrow we shall first go near the city and examine its defenses, then discuss the matter further.” Song Jiang drank until evening, longing for daybreak so that he might go inspect the city. Wu Yong cautioned him, “With two great tigers confined in their prison, how could the city fail to take precautions? We must not go to inspect it by daylight. The moon will surely be bright tonight. If we descend the mountain around the hour of the monkey, we can reach the place by the first watch and observe it secretly.”

p.src: One peak is named Immortal’s Palm, and the Cloud Terrace Temple lies hidden away. Above it joins the Jade Maiden’s Hair-Washing Basin; below it meets the branching waters of the River of Heaven. All heaven and earth are filled with beauty; the pointed peaks seem joined to the very roots of the clouds; Revered above all mountains, its strange crags soar majestically toward the handle of the Dipper. Green as clear-painted brows, azure as floating indigo. Even Zhang Sengyou’s wondrous brush could not paint it, nor could Li Longmian’s inspired genius portray it. From profound grottoes, moonlight scatters ten thousand rays of golden radiance; Across sheer and towering cliffs, sunlight kindles a thousand streams of purple flame. People point from afar, saying the lotus roots in Cloud Pool are as large as boats; Old men relate that the flowers in the Jade Well rise a hundred feet. In his fury, the Mighty Spirit God split open the mountaintop to display his divine power; In his lofty purity, the Recluse Chen built a thatched hermitage there and slept. Through the ages, Mount Hua has been acclaimed in fame; for ten thousand years, incense has burned in worship of Jintian.

p.src: Within two days, a man suddenly came up the mountain and reported, “The court has dispatched a Grand Commandant of the Palace Command, who is bringing the imperially bestowed ‘Golden Bells and Pendants’ to offer incense at the Western Sacred Peak. He is coming by way of the Yellow River and then the Wei River.” When Wu Yong heard this, he said, “Brother, worry no more. Here is the plan we need.” He then summoned Li Jun and Zhang Shun. “You two are to proceed thus and thus for me. …” Li Jun said, “The only difficulty is that no one knows the country there. It would be best to have someone guide us along the way.” Yang Chun, the White-Flowered Snake, said, “How would it be if I went along to help?” Song Jiang was delighted. The three men descended the mountain. The next day, Scholar Wu summoned Song Jiang, Li Ying, Zhu Tong, Huyan Zhuo, Hua Rong, Qin Ming, and Xu Ning—the seven of them—and quietly led just over five hundred men down the mountain. They went straight to the Wei River ferry, where Li Jun, Zhang Shun, and Yang Chun had already seized more than ten large boats. Wu Yong ordered Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Xu Ning, and Huyan Zhuo to lie in ambush on the bank; Song Jiang, Wu Yong, Zhu Tong, and Li Ying boarded the boats; and Li Jun, Zhang Shun, and Yang Chun took all the boats and concealed them by the shoals.

p.src: They all waited through the night. At daybreak the next morning, they heard gongs and drums sounding in the distance. Three official vessels approached, one of them flying a yellow banner inscribed: “Su Yuanjing, Grand Commandant, reverently bearing the imperial decree to offer incense at the Western Sacred Peak.” At the sight, Song Jiang rejoiced inwardly. “The Mystic Maiden once told me, ‘When you meet Su, joy upon joy shall come.’ Now that I have seen this man today, some means will surely present itself.” As the Grand Commandant’s official vessel neared the river mouth, Zhu Tong and Li Ying each took up a long spear and stood behind Song Jiang and Wu Yong. Their boat blocked the Grand Commandant’s vessel in the channel. More than twenty guards in purple robes and silver belts emerged from the vessel and shouted, “What boat are you? How dare you block the channel and obstruct a minister of state?” Holding his mace, Song Jiang bowed and offered a respectful greeting. Standing at the bow, Scholar Wu declared, “Song Jiang, a righteous man of Liangshan Marsh, respectfully presents himself and awaits your command.” The chief steward emerged from the vessel and replied, “This is a Grand Commandant of the imperial court, proceeding under sacred decree to offer incense at the Western Sacred Peak. You are rebels of Liangshan Marsh. Why have you barred our way?” Wu Yong said, “We righteous men ask only to behold the Grand Commandant’s honored countenance, for we have a matter to report.” The chief steward said, “What sort of men are you, to presume to demand an audience with the Grand Commandant?” The guards on either side shouted, “Silence!” Song Jiang said, “We ask the Grand Commandant to come ashore for a short while. There is a matter we must discuss.” The chief steward said, “Enough of this nonsense! The Grand Commandant is a minister commissioned by the court. How could he have anything to discuss with you?” Song Jiang said, “If the Grand Commandant refuses to meet us, I fear my lads may startle His Excellency.” Zhu Tong gave a single wave of the small signal flag fixed to his spear. Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Xu Ning, and Huyan Zhuo led the cavalry out from the bank; all nocked arrows to their bows, advanced to the river mouth, and formed ranks along the shore. The boatmen aboard the vessel were so terrified that they scrambled into the cabins. The chief steward panicked and had no choice but to send someone to report the matter. Grand Commandant Su was obliged to come out, take his seat at the bow, and face them. Song Jiang bowed and respectfully greeted him, saying, “Song Jiang and his companions would never dare behave presumptuously.” Grand Commandant Su said, “Righteous gentlemen, why have you intercepted my vessels in this fashion?” Song Jiang replied, “How would we dare intercept Your Excellency? We wish only to invite you ashore, for there is another matter we must report.” Grand Commandant Su said, “I am now proceeding under a special imperial decree to offer incense at the Western Sacred Peak. What could I have to discuss with you righteous gentlemen? How could a minister of the court lightly set foot ashore?” Song Jiang said, “If Your Excellency refuses, I fear our companions downstream will not let the matter rest.” Li Ying waved the signal pennant on his spear, and Li Jun, Zhang Shun, and Yang Chun all poled their boats into view. Grand Commandant Su was greatly alarmed at the sight. Li Jun and Zhang Shun drew gleaming daggers, leapt aboard the official vessel, and with two swift blows sent two guards tumbling into the water. Song Jiang hurriedly shouted, “No recklessness! Do not frighten His Excellency!” Li Jun and Zhang Shun plunged into the water and promptly lifted the two guards back aboard. Moving over the water as though walking on level ground, Zhang Shun and Li Jun sprang back aboard in an instant. Grand Commandant Su was frightened nearly out of his wits. Song Jiang shouted, “Lads, withdraw for now! Do not frighten His Excellency. I shall respectfully persuade the Grand Commandant to come ashore in my own good time.” Grand Commandant Su asked, “What business have you righteous gentlemen? You may as well tell me here.” Song Jiang replied, “This is no place for such a conversation. I respectfully invite Your Excellency to our stronghold so that I may make my report. We harbor no thought of harming you. If we entertain any such intent, may the divine powers of the Western Sacred Peak strike us dead!” By this point they would not permit the Grand Commandant to remain aboard, so Grand Commandant Su had no choice but to leave his vessel and go ashore. The men brought over a horse and helped the Grand Commandant mount. Having no alternative, he accompanied them. Song Jiang first ordered Hua Rong and Qin Ming to escort the Grand Commandant up the mountain.

p.src: When all the chieftains had reached the mountain, Song Jiang dismounted and entered the stronghold. He helped Grand Commandant Su to the center seat in the Hall of Righteous Assembly, while the chieftains stood in attendance on either side. Song Jiang made four obeisances, knelt before him, and reported, “I was originally a minor clerk in Yuncheng County. Driven beyond endurance by the authorities, I had no choice but to gather men in the greenwood and take temporary refuge amid the waters of Liangshan Marsh. I have waited only for the court to offer amnesty, so that I might serve the country. Now two of my brothers, though guilty of nothing, have been maliciously framed by Prefect He and cast into prison. We wish to borrow Your Excellency’s imperial incense, ceremonial retinue, and ‘Golden Bells and Pendants’ to gain entry to Huazhou by stratagem. Once the affair is concluded, we shall return them all, and no harm whatever shall come to Your Excellency. I beg Your Excellency’s wise consideration.” Grand Commandant Su said, “If you take away the imperial incense and the other articles, once the affair comes to light tomorrow, this humble official will inevitably be implicated.” Song Jiang said, “When Your Excellency returns to the capital, simply lay all the blame upon Song Jiang.” After looking at the fierce bearing of that company, how could Grand Commandant Su possibly refuse? He had no choice but to consent. Song Jiang personally offered him cups of wine, laid out a banquet, and bowed in thanks. They then borrowed and put on all the garments worn by the men who had accompanied the Grand Commandant. From among the lesser bandits they selected a handsome young fellow, shaved off his beard and whiskers, dressed him in the Grand Commandant’s robes, and disguised him as Su Yuanjing; Song Jiang and Wu Yong disguised themselves as chief stewards; Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Yang Xiong, and Shi Xiu disguised themselves as guards; the lesser bandits all donned purple robes and silver belts, carrying ceremonial standards, banners, insignia, ritual objects, and the imperial incense, sacrificial offerings, and ‘Golden Bells and Pendants’; and Hua Rong, Xu Ning, Zhu Tong, and Li Ying disguised themselves as four yamen soldiers. Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun kept the Grand Commandant and his entire retinue at the stronghold, entertaining them with wine. Qin Ming and Huyan Zhuo were ordered to lead one body of troops, while Lin Chong and Yang Zhi led another, the two forces taking separate routes to seize the city. Wu Song was sent ahead to wait beneath the Western Sacred Peak gate and take action only when the signal was given.

Grand Commandant Su said, “If you take away the imperial incense and the other articles, once the affair comes to light tomorrow, this humble official will inevitably be implicated.”
Song Jiang said, “When Your Excellency returns to the capital, simply lay all the blame upon Song Jiang.”
After looking at the fierce bearing of that company, how could Grand Commandant Su possibly refuse?
He had no choice but to consent.
Song Jiang personally offered him cups of wine, laid out a banquet, and bowed in thanks.
They then borrowed and put on all the garments worn by the men who had accompanied the Grand Commandant.
From among the lesser bandits they selected a handsome young fellow, shaved off his beard and whiskers, dressed him in the Grand Commandant’s robes, and disguised him as Su Yuanjing;
Song Jiang and Wu Yong disguised themselves as chief stewards;
Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Yang Xiong, and Shi Xiu disguised themselves as guards;

Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun kept the Grand Commandant and his entire retinue at the stronghold, entertaining them with wine.
Qin Ming and Huyan Zhuo were ordered to lead one body of troops, while Lin Chong and Yang Zhi led another, the two forces taking separate routes to seize the city.
Wu Song was sent ahead to wait beneath the Western Sacred Peak gate and take action only when the signal was given.

p.src: But let us leave needless detail aside. The company departed from the stronghold, went straight to the river mouth, and boarded their boats. Without notifying the prefect of Huazhou, they made directly for the Temple of the Western Peak. Dai Zong went ahead to notify the abbot of Yuntai Abbey and the temple officials, who came all the way to the boats to welcome the party ashore. Incense, flowers, lamps, candles, banners, streamers, and jeweled canopies were arrayed in front. First the imperial incense was placed in an incense pavilion, which the temple bearers shouldered, while the Golden-Bell Hangings were borne at the head of the procession. The abbot paid his respects to the Grand Commandant. Scholar Wu said, “The Grand Commandant has fallen ill on the journey and is unwell. Bring a sedan chair at once.” The attendants supported the Grand Commandant into the chair and carried him straight to the official lodge within the Peak Temple to rest. Scholar Wu, posing as the reception officer, said to the abbot, “We have come expressly under imperial decree, bearing the imperial incense and the Golden-Bell Hangings as offerings to the Holy Emperor. Why have the officials of this prefecture shown such disrespect and failed to come welcome us?” The abbot replied, “We have already sent someone to report your arrival. They should be here at any moment.” Before he had finished speaking, the prefecture sent an assistant judge with fifty or seventy constables, bearing wine and fruit, to pay respects to the Grand Commandant. The young bandit playing the Grand Commandant did resemble him in appearance, but could not imitate his speech or manner of giving orders. They therefore had him feign illness and sit on a bed surrounded by cushions and bolsters. The assistant judge inspected the standards, gate banners, ceremonial guards, and other articles they had brought. All were products of the imperial workshops, so how could he doubt them? The supposed reception officer made a show of going in and out to report twice, then led the assistant judge inside, where he prostrated himself at a distance below the steps. The false Grand Commandant merely pointed with his hand and paid no heed to whatever was said. Wu Yong brought the assistant judge forward and reproached him: “The Grand Commandant is a favored minister close to the Son of Heaven. Sparing himself no hardship over a journey of a thousand li, he came here expressly by imperial decree to offer incense. Yet he unexpectedly fell ill on the road and has not recovered. Why did none of your prefecture’s officials come out to meet him from afar?” The assistant judge replied, “Although dispatches reached the prefecture from the authorities farther along the road, no recent notice arrived, and so we failed to welcome you. We did not expect the Grand Commandant to reach the temple first. The prefect himself should have come, but bandits from Mount Shaohua have joined forces with the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh and intend to attack the city. He must remain on guard against them every day and therefore dares not leave his post without permission. He has sent this humble official ahead to present wine and ceremonial gifts, and will soon follow to pay his respects.” Scholar Wu said, “The Grand Commandant will not drink so much as a drop. Simply tell the prefect to come quickly and discuss the ceremony.” The assistant judge at once ordered the wine brought out and exchanged cups with the reception officer and his attendants. Scholar Wu went inside once more to make a report, then emerged with a key and led the assistant judge to inspect the Golden-Bell Hangings. He unlocked the chest, took the imperially bestowed hangings from their incense-silk bag, showed them to the judge, and had them raised on a bamboo pole. When he looked, its workmanship was indeed beyond compare. This was what he saw:

p.src: This pair of Golden-Bell Hangings had been made by master craftsmen of the imperial workshops in the Eastern Capital. They were fashioned entirely with the seven treasures and pearls, and at their center burned crimson-gauze lanterns shaped like bowls. Intended to hang at the very center of the Holy Emperor’s hall, they could never have been made by common folk unless bestowed from the palace. After letting the assistant judge inspect them, Wu Yong replaced them in their case and locked it. He also produced a large number of official documents from the Secretariat and handed them to the assistant judge. He told him to summon the prefect so they could confer and choose a day for the sacrifice. Having seen all those objects and credentials, the assistant judge and the many constables took leave of the reception officer and returned directly to the Huazhou prefectural offices to report to Prefect He.

p.src: Song Jiang secretly applauded: “Though that rogue is cunning and crafty, we have still dazzled his eyes and thrown his mind into confusion.” By then Wu Song had already taken up position at the temple gate. Scholar Wu also had Shi Xiu conceal a sharp knife and go to the temple gate to help Wu Song carry out the plan; and he had Dai Zong disguise himself as a military aide. The abbot of Yuntai Abbey presented a vegetarian meal while directing the officiants to arrange and adorn the Peak Temple. Song Jiang strolled about inspecting the Temple of the Western Peak. It was splendidly constructed, its halls extraordinary—a veritable heaven in the mortal world. Song Jiang entered the main hall, pinched incense between his fingers, and bowed twice. After silently praying, he returned to the front of the official lodge. p.src: Now Prefect He brought more than three hundred men with him. Reaching the temple, he dismounted before the gate and entered surrounded by his followers. Scholar Wu, posing as the reception officer, and Song Jiang saw that the prefect had entered with over three hundred men, all constables and clerks wearing swords. Scholar Wu shouted, “The court’s Grand Commandant is here! No unauthorized person may approach!” The crowd stopped in its tracks. Prefect He alone stepped forward to pay his respects to the Grand Commandant. The reception officer said, “The Grand Commandant bids the prefect come in and meet him.” Prefect He entered the official lodge and bowed toward the false Grand Commandant. Scholar Wu said, “Prefect, do you know your crime?” The prefect replied, “I, He, did not know the Grand Commandant had arrived. I humbly beg forgiveness.” Scholar Wu said, “The Grand Commandant came by imperial command to offer incense at the Western Peak. Why did you not go out to meet him from afar?” The prefect replied, “No recent notice reached the prefecture, and so we failed to welcome you.” Scholar Wu shouted, “Seize him!” The brothers Xie Zhen and Xie Bao had already whipped short blades from their clothes. They kicked Prefect He to the floor and cut off his head. Song Jiang shouted, “Brothers, strike!” The more than three hundred followers were so terrified that they stood stupefied, unable even to flee. Hua Rong and the others rushed forward together and knocked the whole company down like counting rods scattered across the ground; Half of them forced their way out through the temple gate, but Wu Song and Shi Xiu came slashing in with their blades while the young bandits pursued and killed them on every side. Of the more than three hundred men, not one returned. Those who arrived later at the temple were all killed by Zhang Shun and Li Jun.

p.src: Song Jiang hurriedly ordered the imperial incense and the hangings gathered up and taken aboard the boats. When they all hastened to Huazhou, they saw fires already rising in two quarters of the city and charged in together. They first went to the prison and rescued Shi Jin and Lu Zhishen; then they broke open the storehouses, took the wealth and valuables, and loaded them onto carts. The company left Huazhou, boarded their boats, and returned to Mount Shaohua. There they all paid respects to Grand Commandant Su and returned the imperial incense, Golden-Bell Hangings, standards, gate banners, ceremonial guards, and other articles, bowing their thanks to their gracious benefactor. Song Jiang ordered a tray of gold and silver brought as a gift for the Grand Commandant. All his attendants, regardless of rank, were also given gold and silver. They held a farewell banquet in the stronghold to thank the Grand Commandant. The chiefs escorted him all the way down the mountain. At the river mouth they handed over every article and every boat, with nothing missing, to the people from whom they had taken them.

p.src: Now Grand Commandant Su came ashore and entered the city of Huazhou. He had already learned that the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh had killed the soldiers and cavalry, plundered the treasury and granaries, slain more than a hundred officers and men in the city, and carried off every horse. Many lives had also been taken in the Temple of the Western Peak. He therefore ordered the judicial officer of the prefecture to draw up a report for submission through the Secretariat to the throne, making the whole affair read: “Song Jiang first seized the imperial incense and ceremonial hangings on the road, then used them to lure the prefect to the temple and murder him.” Grand Commandant Su burned the imperial incense in the temple and entrusted the golden-belled ceremonial hangings to the abbot of Yuntai Monastery. He then hurried back to the capital by night to report the affair to the throne. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: The next day, Shi Jin, Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun each contributed from his own purse to hold a banquet in gratitude to Lords Chao and Song and all the chiefs. Several days passed. Let us waste no more words on this. Then one day Zhu Gui, the “Dry-Land Crocodile,” came up the mountain and reported: “A new band of outlaws has gathered on Mount Mangdang in Pei County, Xuzhou, with three thousand men and horses. Their principal leader is a man named Fan Rui, nicknamed the “Demon King of Chaos.” He can summon wind and rain, and commands troops with divine skill. He has two lieutenants. One is Xiang Chong, nicknamed the “Eight-Armed Nezha.” He carries a round shield fitted with twenty-four throwing knives and wields an iron javelin in his hand. The other is Li Gun, nicknamed the “Flying Great Sage.” He too carries a round shield, fitted with twenty-four javelins, and wields a fine sword. The three have sworn brotherhood, occupied Mount Mangdang, and make their living by raiding homes and robbing travelers. They have conferred together and mean to come annex our great stronghold at Liangshan Marsh. When I heard this, I could not but report it.” Song Jiang was furious when he heard this. “How dare those knaves show such insolence! I shall go down the mountain once more myself!” At once Shi Jin, the “Nine-Dragoned,” rose and said: “The four of us have only just arrived at the great stronghold and have not earned the slightest merit. We willingly ask to lead our own troops and capture this band of outlaws.” Song Jiang was delighted. Shi Jin immediately mustered his own troops. He, Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun donned their armor and went to take leave of Song Jiang before descending the mountain; they crossed Golden Sand Beach by boat, took to the road, and headed straight for Mount Mangdang.

p.src: The two men immediately descended the mountain on foot. Seeing Shi Jin, Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun mounted before the opposing ranks, they exchanged not a word. As the lesser bandits struck up their gongs, the two heroes brandished their round shields and rolled straight into the formation together. Shi Jin and the others could not hold them back, and the rear ranks were the first to flee. Shi Jin's vanguard tried to resist, while Zhu Wu and the others raised battle cries in the center, but the troops broke and scattered. Truly, though the men might wish to stand, their horses would not; they were driven back thirty or forty li. Shi Jin narrowly escaped being struck by a flying dagger. Yang Chun was slow in turning back, and a flying dagger wounded his warhorse. He abandoned the horse and fled for his life. When Shi Jin mustered his troops, he found that half had been lost. He consulted Zhu Wu and the others about sending someone back to Liangshan Marsh to seek reinforcements. While they were still anxiously wavering, a soldier came to report: “A cloud of dust has risen on the northern highway. Some two thousand troops and horsemen appear to be approaching.” Shi Jin and the others went straight out to meet them and discovered the banners of Liangshan Marsh. At the head rode two great commanders: “Little Li Guang” Hua Rong and “Golden-Lance Bearer” Xu Ning. Shi Jin received them and gave a full account of how Xiang Chong and Li Gun rolled forward behind their savage shields and could not be stopped by his troops. Hua Rong said, “Brother Song Gongming was deeply worried when he saw that you had come here, elder brother, and bitterly regretted letting you go. He therefore sent the two of us especially to assist you.” Shi Jin and the others were overjoyed. They joined their forces and made camp together. At daybreak the next morning, just as they were preparing to march out against the enemy, a soldier reported: “Another force is approaching along the northern highway.” When Hua Rong, Xu Ning, and Shi Jin mounted together and rode out to meet them, they found Song Gongming himself arriving with the strategist Scholar Wu, Gongsun Sheng, Chai Jin, Zhu Tong, Huyan Zhuo, Mu Hong, Sun Li, Huang Xin, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng at the head of three thousand troops. Shi Jin related in detail how Xiang Chong and Li Gun had used flying daggers, javelins, and rolling shields that no one could approach, causing him to lose men and horses. Song Jiang was greatly alarmed, but Wu Yong said, “Let us first encamp the troops behind a stockade, then consider another plan.” Impatient by nature, Song Jiang insisted on raising the troops to destroy and capture the bandits, and marched straight to the foot of the mountain. By then night had fallen, and they saw that Mount Mangdang was covered with blue-green lanterns. Gongsun Sheng looked at them and said, “These blue-green lanterns within the stronghold show that there must be someone inside who practices sorcery. For now, let us withdraw our troops. Tomorrow this poor Daoist will present a battle formation with which to capture those two men.” Song Jiang was delighted and gave orders for the troops to withdraw twenty li and pitch camp there. Early the next morning, Gongsun Sheng revealed his battle formation. And thus it came to pass that the Demon Kings would submit and ascend Liangshan, while the Divine Generals would give their hearts to the marsh stronghold. But what battle formation did Gongsun Sheng present? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
